reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: All 3 gates passed. Gate 1 skipped (missing-validation finding: absent WITH CHECK column restriction is the issue, not dead code). Gate 2: no trust_assumptions in scope file; attack vector is Supabase REST API with attacker's own valid JWT — no trusted-source exception applies. Gate 3: supabase/migrations/ is explicitly in scope and admin role enforcement is a listed key concern. Verified in 0000_create_member_schema.sql L83: policy is `USING (auth.uid() = id)` with no WITH CHECK clause, while L16 grants ALL on tables to authenticated, including UPDATE on is_admin. The 20260317000001_fix_security_permissions.sql patch only revoked anon access and applied FORCE RLS; it left this policy unchanged. An attacker can trigger this via the Supabase REST API by sending PATCH /rest/v1/member.members?id=eq.<attacker-uuid> with body {"is_admin": true} using their own Supabase JWT, causing full privilege escalation to admin because the RLS USING clause (auth.uid() = id) is satisfied and no WITH CHECK restriction blocks the is_admin column write.
